column1: # reviewer-message-classes.tsv — per-bot message classes for the reviewer scorecard (#2504).
# and used by scripts/reviewer_report.sh alone. The advisory approval gate and the
# maintainer-comment gate never read this file, so adding or changing a row here cannot
# change who blocks or clears a merge.
# Why a sidecar and not a column in reviewer-sources.tsv: that registry has a fixed
# positional schema (rationale is column 7) read by five consumers, both gates included,
# and one row per bot. A bot here needs several patterns across several classes and
# message kinds. The registry patterns also match the markdown `body`, but the scorecard
# reads GraphQL `bodyText`, where HTML comments and markdown markup are already stripped.
#   login   — the bot's GraphQL App login (no "[bot]" suffix). Must be a registered
#   class   — finding | clean | refused | skipped | status
#               finding  — the bot raised at least one problem.
#               clean    — the bot reviewed and found nothing.
#               refused  — the bot declined because of quota, rate limit, trial or plan.
#               skipped  — the bot did not review because of its own or the repo's config.
#               status   — progress, summary, marketing or bookkeeping text; no verdict.
#             (`unclassified` is never written here: it is what a message gets when no
#             row, the shared fallback or a structural default matches it.)
#   kind    — any | review | inline | issue | check_run — which message kind the row applies to.
#               review = PR review body, inline = review-thread comment,
#               issue = top-level PR comment, check_run = the check-run summary.
#   pattern — a jq/Oniguruma regex, matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY against the message's
#             bodyText (or a check run's output summary). Unanchored unless you anchor it.
#   1. this bot's rows, top to bottom — the FIRST row that matches wins, so put the
#      narrow rows (a refusal inside a summary, a finding marker) above the broad ones.
#      Bot rows of any class now apply to inline comments when kind is "inline" or "any".
#   2. the shared refusal fallback — ADVISORY_RATE_LIMIT_RE from advisory-review-gate.sh
#      plus its author-scoped cubic clause (never applied to inline comments);
#   3. structural defaults in reviewer_report.sh — the first inline comment of a thread
#      is a finding, a later one is status; a CHANGES_REQUESTED review is a finding and an
#      APPROVED one is clean; a successful check run is clean;
#   4. otherwise `unclassified`. The report shows up to 3 samples per bot, so a new
#      message shape is visible and can be given a row here.
